summary: Provides a YANG data model for virtual network operations, where a provider offers customers a network to use as if it were physical. It applies generally and includes operations as in the ACTN framework of RFC 8453.

eli5.summary: A company can rent a pretend network that behaves like its own. This gives a standard way to order and manage it.

questions: yang model for virtual network operations
what is the ietf-vn yang module
what does the vn-compute rpc do
subtitle: A YANG model that lets a customer order, inspect and compute a provider-built virtual network as a single object.

tldr.problem: A service provider can offer a customer a Virtual Network (VN) to use as though it were a physical network, but the customer and provider need a standard data model for describing and managing it.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-vn YANG module describes Access Points, VN Access Points and VNs made of VN members, and refers to abstract nodes in the TE Topology model. It also defines a vn-compute RPC to compute a VN before creating it.
tldr.outcome: The model is generally applicable to any mode of VN operation, with ACTN as its primary example, and can work alongside service models such as L3SM, L2SM and L1CSM.

today: RFC 9731 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2025. It has not been obsoleted or updated according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: What the VN Model Provides
sections.content:
A Virtual Network (VN) is a network a provider gives a customer to use in any way it wants, as though it were physical. In the Abstraction and Control of TE Networks (ACTN) framework (RFC 8453), a VN is built from abstractions of underlying Traffic Engineered (TE) networks. This RFC defines a YANG data model (RFC 7950) for it. ACTN is the main example, but the model is not limited to it.

The model describes three things: Access Points (APs), which are the customer's endpoint characteristics; VN Access Points (VNAPs), which describe how an AP is partitioned among several VNs and refer to a Link Termination Point (LTP) of the provider edge node; and the VNs themselves, made of VN members with multi-source and multi-destination characteristics and a reference to an abstract node in the TE topology.

It can stand alone or work with customer service models such as the L3VPN Service Model (RFC 8299) and the L2VPN Service Model (RFC 8466). Operational state is in the same tree as configuration, consistent with the Network Management Datastore Architecture (RFC 8342).
sections.eli5: The model has three kinds of paperwork: where the customer plugs in, how a plug is shared among several rented networks, and the rented network itself, made of several routes between plugs.

sections.title: Type 1 and Type 2 VNs
sections.content:
In the ACTN setting, the customer's controller (the CNC) talks to the provider's Multi-Domain Service Coordinator (MDSC) across the CNC-MDSC Interface (CMI), using both the VN model and the TE Topology model (RFC 8795).

A Type 1 VN is a set of edge-to-edge abstract links. Each link is a VN member, formed as an end-to-end tunnel across the underlying networks. The RFC's example has four members: L1-L4, L1-L7, L2-L4 and L3-L8, modeled as one abstract node, AN1, with a connectivity matrix entry per member.

A Type 2 VN adds an underlay topology so the customer can choose the path for some members. In the example, VN member 1 (L1-L4) selects the explicit path {S3,S4,S5} through an underlay of nodes S1 to S11. A Type 1 VN can be seen as a higher-level abstraction of a Type 2 VN. The underlay may be a native or abstract TE topology, and the topologies can be agreed between CNC and MDSC beforehand or created during VN instantiation.
sections.eli5: Type 1 is like ordering a train ticket from city A to city B and letting the railway pick the route. Type 2 is when you say which stations you want to pass through.

sections.title: Control Flows Between Customer and Provider
sections.content:
For a Type 1 VN, the CNC first posts the TE Topology model with a connectivity matrix on one abstract node, then posts the VN identifying the AP, VNAPs and VN members and mapping them to the TE topology. Finally it can GET the VN status. If a member has multiple sources or destinations, the MDSC selects one and updates the VN.

For a Type 2 VN there are two cases. In Case 1 the CNC creates the single abstract node topology, with explicit paths in the connectivity matrix, before posting the VN. In Case 2 the CNC posts the VN first, the MDSC populates a single abstract node topology itself, and the CNC then posts the TE topology with the connectivity matrix and explicit paths.

The customer access may not be known at VN creation. The operation allows creating a VN with only a PE identifier, since the ap container has a leaf for the pe node, and the customer access information can be added later.
sections.eli5: The customer first sends the map of what they want, then the order, then checks on the order. Sometimes the provider draws the map itself, and the customer then adds the exact route.

sections.title: Usage Patterns and VN Compute
sections.content:
The model lets a customer see grouped edge-to-edge links as one entity, similar to the separate customer service models described in RFC 8309. A VN does not have to be configured explicitly: the MDSC can create one automatically from the customer service model and local policy, and the CNC can still use the VN model to learn its details.

The vn-compute RPC supports VN compute, a pre-instantiation mode that shows the full VN as a single entity before it exists. The input can carry path constraints and optimization criteria at VN level and VN-member level, with member-level values overriding VN-level ones, plus VN policies. The MDSC computes the result without creating a VN or reserving resources. The output refers to the single abstract node topology, gives each member a reference to its connectivity matrix entry, and includes error information if something fails.

For multiple sources and destinations, a member can list several candidates when the best choice depends on network resource conditions. The model records which one was selected in an if-selected leaf, available through the multi-src-dest feature.
sections.eli5: Before you rent the network you can ask the provider "what would it look like?" and get an answer without anything being reserved. It is like getting a price quote before booking.

sections.title: The ietf-vn Module
sections.content:
The module is named ietf-vn with prefix vn and sits under a top-level virtual-network container holding a list of VNs keyed by id. Each VN has a te-topology-identifier (provider ID, client ID, topology ID), an optional reference to an abstract node, and a list of VN members. Each member has a src and dest naming an AP and VNAP, and a connectivity-matrix-id pointing into the TE topology.

The module imports types from ietf-yang-types, ietf-network, ietf-network-topology, ietf-te-types and ietf-te-topology. The RFC also gives JSON examples in an appendix for both the VN model and the TE Topology connectivity matrix, and an appendix on performance constraints.
sections.eli5: The module is a big form. At the top is the list of rented networks, and each one lists its routes from one plug to another.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is accessed through management protocols such as NETCONF or RESTCONF. Their mandatory-to-implement secure transports are SSH and TLS, and the Network Configuration Access Control Model (RFC 8341) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

On the CMI, the RFC lists risks such as malicious attack, rogue elements trying to connect, policy conflicts and eavesdropping. Some ACTN components, such as the MDSC, are a single point of failure and threat vector.

Writable nodes in the ap, vn-ap, vn and vn-member lists are sensitive because an attacker able to change them may manipulate the VN. Readable nodes such as oper-status and if-selected can reveal operational state and which source or destination was selected. The vn-compute RPC can reveal VN information, so access to it should be controlled.
sections.eli5: The order forms and status sheets can be abused if strangers can write on them or read them, so only trusted people should get access, over a protected line.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA has registered the XML namespace URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-vn in the IETF XML Registry, with the IESG as registrant. It has also registered the module in the YANG Module Names registry with name ietf-vn, prefix vn and reference RFC 9731.
sections.eli5: The module's name was written in the official list of names so nobody else uses it.
